Let's bring it up in the PeerDAS breakout + advertise correct cgc when fulu fork epoch < far away epoch <Leobago> There is a backfill session after the peerDAS session <Leobago> BTW, i was asked to share this here: https://ethresear.ch/t/a-new-design-for-das-and-sharded-blob-mempools/22537 https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4373 Actually I'm not sure if it should be done in status or metadata. The issue is if we do it status, a the peer could think that the updated cgc in ENR/metadata corresponds to the (old) value in status. (Prysm requires status twice per epoch.) Also pinged all cl devs so we do enr before fulu and metadata after, i think that is ok? > update CGC immediately > optional backfill if we update cgc immediately and keep backfill optional, are we not preparing for a potential downscoring spree? There’s a new proposal to add a lowest_block_epoch field to status message to address that. Just had a breakout and seems like a good solution without introducing too much complexity. So if a node increases CGC, and advertise it immediately, they’d update lowest_block_epoch to the current epoch, to indicate they only have the advertise columns from this point. So peers would not Downscore them from not having columns before this epoch. If the node chooses to backfill, then it will update this field as they progress with backfill. Happy to create a spec PR tomorrow morning if no one gets to it. <@412614104222531604> <@531934490826768418> Thanks for volunteering <@412614104222531604> 🤗 alright He might not see msgs for a bit, feel free to commit him to other tasks 😂 Proposal <@&1367819082019377202> : https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4374 **Note 1:** This proposal does not take into account the <@833706406699073536> 's idea about bitmasks to allow beacon nodes to convey different coverage ranges for different sets of columns. Could you tell more about it? **Note 2:** Issue from <@293154341127454721>: If a malicious peer advertises a given `cgc`, but keeps maintaining its `lowest_slot` equals to `head_slot`, then the malicious peer will never have to actually serve any sidecar, without being penalized. This is the idea resulting from the breakout session.

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content:
Actually I'm not sure if it should be done in status or metadata.
The issue is if we do it status, a the peer could think that the updated cgc in ENR/metadata corresponds to the (old) value in status.
(Prysm requires status twice per epoch.)

Proposal <@&1367819082019377202> :
https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4374

**Note 1:** This proposal does not take into account the <@833706406699073536> 's idea about bitmasks to allow beacon nodes to convey different coverage ranges for different sets of columns. Could you tell more about it?
**Note 2:** Issue from <@293154341127454721>: If a malicious peer advertises a given `cgc`, but keeps maintaining its `lowest_slot` equals to `head_slot`, then the malicious peer will never have to actually serve any sidecar, without being penalized.

This is the idea resulting from the breakout session.
